newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kubo says no report on Nomura paying client losses.
newsitem.headline: Kubo says no report on Nomura paying client losses.

text.p: Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Wednesday he had received no report on a newspaper article saying Nomura Securities Co Ltd had been questioned on suspicion of compensating a corporate client for losses.
"I have not received any report on it," Kubo told a news conference when asked about the newspaper article.
Earlier, Nomura denied a report in regional daily Hokkaido Shimbun which said the brokerage was suspected of having paid the client compensation of up to several hundred million yen.

Nomura's public relations office said in a statement it was untrue a Nomura executive had been questioned by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) and that there had been no deals such as those referred to by the paper.
The paper quoted the SESC and industry sources as saying one of Nomura's corporate customers placed futures orders in Singapore markets through Nomura in 1994.
These deals resulted in a loss of several hundred million yen and Nomura tried to offset this loss by raising profits through trading shares for the customer, the paper said.
Nomura said it had made an internal investigation which showed that neither the Singapore futures deal nor the ensuing compensation cited in the newspaper had taken place.
